clue.text: React badly when taken in by one scientist or another

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so the jumbled letters sit within the other word

parts.note: after 'one scientist', 'another' scientist here is a student of living things

indicators.note: react done badly is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist reacts poorly on being taken in by a rival researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one scientist or another' reads as one phrase, but splits: the answer is one scientist and 'another' supplies a different one. 'badly' makes ACTER, which 'when taken in by' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacteriologist is a specialist who studies bacteria, one kind of scientist among many.

clue.text: Rural sort of business man gets round city in Sicily

parts.note: agri- is the farming prefix of agribusiness, the rural kind of business
a gent is a man
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A farming businessman travels around a Sicilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrigento is a town on the south coast of Sicily, famed for its Greek temples.

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece applauds a runner in a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, as is 'cheers'. Marathon is a Greek place, so its characters are Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character used in Greek writing.

clue.text: After composition, Grieg used to prepare for rough treatment

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the two words are recomposed

explanation.surface: Grieg, having written a piece, was used to rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: Grieg the composer makes 'composition' look musical, but 'After composition' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruggedise equipment is to make it tough enough to survive harsh use.

clue.text: Norma, say, in post office, turning up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits below it
in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A woman named Norma appears in a post office, arriving punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes OP of PO; ERA is placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's opera, so it is an example of the form.

indicators.note: the words are forced into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A savage is compelled to go without.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were a Germanic tribe that overran Italy, the sort of people the Romans called barbarians.

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
nuit is the French word for night

explanation.surface: Someone from the north spends a night overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous people of the Arctic, so people from the far north.

clue.text: Because of that your beer is brewed inside

indicators.note: the brewed word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: brewing turns ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Your beer is being made indoors, for that reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' makes EREB, the anagram signal; 'inside' places it within the archaic word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means, as a result of it.

clue.text: Shopping area in centre of Brussels supplies underwear

indicators.note: the shopping area sits in the middle letters taken from the city's name
the centre of the word Brussels is its middle pair of letters

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A Brussels shopping centre stocks underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle pair from Brussels and 'in' wraps it round the shopping area. Smalls is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is British informal for small items of clothing, especially knickers and pants.

explanation.surface: A spread laid out for a cartoon housewife.
explanation.definitionFit: Marge is British short for margarine, a butter substitute, and Marge is Homer's wife in the TV cartoon The Simpsons.

clue.text: Game bird with swallow in river

indicators.note: the swallowing word goes in the bird

parts.note: a grouse is a game bird
to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: A game bird with a swallow inside it, found by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like another bird but is the verb. The Great Ouse is a river in eastern England flowing past Bedford and Ely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Ouse is a long river in eastern England that drains into the Wash.

clue.text: Silver, boarding vessel, runs away with cases

indicators.note: silver boards the boat, going inside it
the runs go away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a lugger is a small sailing boat
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver is loaded on a ship and the crew flee carrying bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' removes R from the boat, leaving LUGGE; 'boarding' puts silver's symbol in it before its final E. 'Silver' tempts as Long John Silver boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is bags and suitcases collectively.

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A missionary turns people with earnest pleas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' fits the missionary's surface but signals the anagram of PLEAS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is someone sent to spread a faith, like the first Christian preachers.

explanation.surface: A god's verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to sense something intuitively, and good sense is sound judgment.

parts.note: to eye is to watch
to dog someone is to follow them, to shadow

explanation.surface: A watchdog for beauty products.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye shadow is coloured make-up applied to the eyelids.

clue.text: Wickedly suggest concealing promises to pay

indicators.note: one word conceals the other by holding it inside

parts.note: to imply is to suggest
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone slyly hints at hiding debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts the debts inside the word for suggest, before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiously means irreverently, without respect for God, hence sinfully.

indicators.note: switch means change around, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A plastic switch is needed for a phone system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a part on the phone, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polythene is a common lightweight plastic used for bags and film.

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
kicks are thrills or fun

explanation.surface: A party with entertainment among close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidekicks are companions or assistants who stick close to someone.

clue.text: Bread for dinner, say, and nothing else?

parts.note: with nothing else left out, the thing is whole and entire
dinner is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: Asking whether bread alone makes a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is made from flour that keeps the entire grain.

clue.text: Celebrate with drinking — and lament holding mug

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to wail is to lament
a mug is a fool or dupe, an ass

explanation.surface: Drinking in celebration but wailing over a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' suggests a drinking vessel to match the wassail, but it means a fool; 'holding' puts it inside, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To wassail is to make merry with plenty of drink, as in old Christmas revelry.

indicators.note: the monster is found in the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A creature lurking in a dirty drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek legend slain by Heracles.

indicators.note: the trial comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A show trial held after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to show or demonstrate that something is true.

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A smasher is literally something that breaks things, and informally a very attractive person, as is a dish.

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailors sit below the trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Trouble with the crew beneath the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like the ship's floor, but it is the verb meaning decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something out is to decorate it.

explanation.surface: A dispute that ends with someone being detained.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or clash, and to run in a suspect is informal for arresting them.

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid
E.T. is the alien of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: A dim alien is filmed in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense group of bushes or trees.

clue.text: Dramatist starts introducing boring scenes entertaining nobody

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A playwright introduces dull scenes that amuse no one.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Advice on a new way to reduce tax

indicators.note: a new form of the words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on a fresh tax-cutting scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram of ADVICE ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax avoidance is lowering what you owe by legal means, unlike evasion.

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud, and a word of the same sound is written

parts.note: a sax is a saxophone, an instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument heard in a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' is the verb meaning dismisses from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the sack is to dismiss them, so it sacks means it fires.

clue.text: Having too much to say about Nelson's wedding

indicators.note: about here means round and about, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the name with its S kept

explanation.surface: Someone talks too much about Nelson's wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but signals rearranging NELSONS WEDDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Longwindedness is wordiness, going on at great length.
